title: Afghanistan’s Taliban government imposes smartphone ban on government officials
byline: Afghanistan’s Taliban government has ordered a nationwide ban on civil servants’ smartphone use, a military court order showed, prompting ​warnings from rights activists that the move could further restrict access ‌to information.

title: Country loses US $ 1 billion in fraudulent transactions, certain banks involved
byline: In a shocking disclosure, President Anura Kumara Dissanayake said in Parliament yesterday that the country had lost as much as US $ 1 billion because of the transfer of a whopping Rs.300 billion ill-gotten cash in terms of Telegraphic Transfers and Advanced Payments for imports. He said that certain banks had been implicated in the fraudulent transactions.

title: At least 40 injured in head-on bus collision in Matara
byline: At least 40 people have been hospitalized following a head-on collision between two private buses along the Matara-Talalla road, police said.

title: Philippines bans video game played by alleged high school shooter
byline: The Philippines has temporarily blocked gaming app Gorebox after an initial investigation found that a teenage suspect in a rare school shooting had been playing the game.

title: UN halts escort of ships through Hormuz after vessel comes under attack
byline: The U.N. International Maritime Organization paused its operation to escort ships through the Strait of Hormuz on Thursday after a vessel reported an attack, reigniting concerns about ‌whether a preliminary deal to end the Iran war will hold.

title: Chief Inspector arrested over death of female physiotherapist
byline: A Chief Inspector of Police has been arrested in connection with the death of a female physiotherapist found inside a car in Teldeniya.

title: Australia considers tougher enforcement of social media ban for teens
byline: Australia’s prime minister ​said on Friday he was keen to make sure the country’s social media ban ‌for children was as strong as possible, as a new study found that the measure — the first of its kind and now six months old — had little impact on teen use.

title: Malaysia deports alleged underworld gunman to Sri Lanka
byline: An alleged underworld gunman linked to organized crime figure Kehelbaddara Padme was deported from Malaysia and taken into custody by Sri Lankan authorities upon his arrival at the Bandaranaike International Airport in Katunayake last night (25).

title: Rescuers search rubble for survivors as Venezuela earthquakes kill at least 235
byline: Rescuers are searching through rubble in a rush to save lives after two powerful earthquakes struck Venezuela near the capital, killing at least 235 people and injuring more than 1,500.

title: Contract farming gains momentum as IFC backs local poultry sector
byline: The local poultry sector is seeing a renewed push towards contract farming and sustainable production, with the International Finance Corporation (IFC) backing an expansion by New Anthony’s Farm Group

title: CCC outlines three-year plan to strengthen  Sri Lanka’s competitiveness
byline: The Ceylon Chamber of Commerce (CCC) yesterday said it is working with a three-year strategy to accelerate investment, boost exports and strengthen support for small businesses, as the private sector seeks to play a larger role in sustaining the country’s economic recovery.

title: Confiscated narcotics to be destroyed in Puttalam tomorrow
byline: A quantity of confiscated narcotics is scheduled to be destroyed tomorrow morning (June 27) at the incinerator facility located at Lactowatta in Wanathavilluwa, Puttalam.

title: Saudi Aramco resumes oil loading at Ras Tanura after 4-month halt
byline: Saudi Aramco resumed oil loading on ​Friday at its Ras Tanura terminal in the Gulf after a near four-month halt, shipping data from LSEG showed, in a sign ‌that Middle Eastern producers are pushing forward with plans to boost exports despite a ship attack in the Strait of Hormuz.

title: Warning over power bank fire risk on flights as summer holidays begin
byline: Flight passengers are being warned not to pack power banks or vapes in their hold luggage ahead of the busy summer holiday travel period beginning for parts of the UK.

title: Opposition MPs sign motion on judicial appointments delay
byline: Opposition MPs began signing a motion today to request for a special debate on the delay in appointing senior judicial officers.

title: President doesn't answer MPs’ phone calls: Dayasiri
byline: President Anura Kumara Dissanayake never answers MPs’ phone calls, Opposition MP Dayasiri Jayasekera told Parliament today.

title: Seven more battery energy storage systems arrive at Colombo Port
byline: A consignment of seven additional Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS) arrived at the Colombo Port yesterday evening.

title: Afghanistan’s Taliban government imposes smartphone ban on government officials
byline: Afghanistan’s Taliban government has ordered a nationwide ban on civil servants’ smartphone use, a military court order showed, prompting ​warnings from rights activists that the move could further restrict access ‌to information.

title: Gnanasara Thera’s case over alleged anti-Islam remarks fixed for July 31
byline: The Colombo High Court today ordered that the case filed by the Attorney General against Bodu Bala Sena (BBS) General Secretary Ven. Galagodaththe Gnanasara Thera, over allegedly insulting Islam be recalled on July 31 for a preliminary trial conference.

title: Govt will control solar power systems by next year: Minister
byline: The government will be able to take control of solar power systems by next year with the fixing of 2,000 modems, Deputy Minister of Power and Energy Akram Ilyas told Parliament today.

title: King Charles III will not live at Buckingham Palace after refurbishment completion
byline: King Charles III will not live at Buckingham Palace after the completion of a 10-year, 369 million-pound (US$487 million) refurbishment programme as the monarchy seeks to increase public access to the historic building that has been the centre of royal life for almost 200 years.

title: SLTB to receive 600 new buses by year-end
byline: The Ministry of Transport and Highways has announced plans to add 600 new buses to the Sri Lanka Transport Board (SLTB) fleet by December in a bid to strengthen public transport services across the country.

title: Large rooftop solar owners asked to disconnect from grid during Poson
byline: As electricity demand is expected to fall during the Poson holidays, owners of rooftop solar systems with a capacity of 300 kW and above have been asked to disconnect from the national grid during daytime from June 27 to 29, Deputy Minister of Energy Arkam Ilyas informed Parliament today.

title: Dayasiri, Kumara Jayakody stage showdown in Parliament
byline: Opposition MP Dayasiri Jayasekera and former Minister of Power and Energy Kumara Jayakody engaged in a heated argument in Parliament on the issue of inferior quality coal.

title: SJB suspends Horana Organiser Charith Abeysinghe
byline: The Samagi Jana Balawegaya (SJB) has taken steps to suspend the party membership of its Horana Organiser, Charith Abeysinghe, following his arrest and subsequent remand over an alleged bribery incident.

title: Sri Lanka Cricket set for final strike
byline: Sri Lanka Cricket is at the threshold of winning the battle for change as the much awaited new Constitution is being put through the finishing touches before it goes to Parliament for approval and the government’s Transformation Committee able to declare its mission is over.

title: Over 90 organised crime suspects still abroad: Minister
byline: A total of 96 organised crime suspects wanted under Interpol Red Notices remain in hiding overseas, with Sri Lankan authorities continuing efforts to bring them back to the country, said Public Security Minister Anand Wijepala.

title: BASL denies making representation for arrested attorney Rakitha Rajapakshe
byline: The Bar Association of Sri Lanka (BASL) has clarified that it neither authorised any Attorney-at-Law to make representations on its behalf nor decided to intervene on behalf of Attorney-at-Law Rakitha Rajapakshe during yesterday’s proceedings before the Colombo Chief Magistrate’s Court.

title: SMEs urged to register for VAT voluntarily to boost growth
byline: The Government has encouraged Small and Medium-sized Enterprises (SMEs) with annual turnovers below the mandatory Value Added Tax (VAT) registration threshold of Rs. 60 million to register voluntarily, highlighting the benefits of doing so.

title: Govt moves to speed up Jaffna land restitution process
byline: The government has decided to speed up the release of state and private lands in Jaffna and Palaly that are currently being used by the security forces.

title: Ajith Vs Asitha argument over Opposition Leader and sister
byline: An argument popped up in Parliament today between Opposition MP Ajith P. Perera and ruling party MP Asitha Niroshana over a case involving Opposition Leader Sajith Premadasa’s sister.

title: ADB approves USD 57m for Sri Lanka rooftop solar aggregation project
byline: The Asian Development Bank (ADB) on Friday said it has approved a USD-57.4-million (EUR 50.4m) financing package for a solar aggregation and virtual net metering project in Sri Lanka.

title: Russia reports large-scale Ukrainian drone attack across 12 regions
byline: Russian air defences intercepted 660 Ukrainian drones in a major nighttime attack on 12 regions as well as the Russia-held Crimean peninsula, the Black Sea and the Azov Sea, Russia’s Defence Ministry said Friday

title: Ireland stun world champions India for historic T20 win
byline: Ireland caused a massive shock as they claimed a first senior international win over world champions India in Friday’s opening T20 international in Belfast.

title: Small aircraft crashes into Beijing’s tallest building
byline: An aircraft about the size of a car crashed ​into Beijing’s tallest building on Friday, witnesses told Reuters, with police closing off roads around the ‌skyscraper and authorities giving no information about the incident.

title: Multi-vehicle collision on Southern Expressway triggers severe traffic congestion
byline: A multi-vehicle collision involving five vehicles occurred on the Southern Expressway today near the 31st kilometer post between the Galanigama and Dodangoda interchanges, causing significant traffic congestion.

title: Fuel price relief likely as global oil prices decline: Govt.
byline: The government is expecting to provide relief to consumers as global fuel prices continue to decline, Deputy Minister of Finance and Planning Dr. Anil Jayantha Fernando said today.

title: Sri Lanka still believe semis within reach at T20 World Cup
byline: There is confidence in Sri Lanka’s defense ahead of their final group match of the Twenty20 World Cup against Scotland, which is set to begin in a few moments.

title: Nuwanidu fights back after Jurel’s Century puts India A on top
byline: Captain Dhruv Jurel’s unbeaten 141 powered India A to a commanding 452 for 6 declared before the visitors struck twice to leave Sri Lanka A on 113 for 2 at stumps on a rain-hit second day of the first unofficial Test in Galle.
